newsitem.title: USA: Drillers rally breaks on Transocean EPS outlook.
newsitem.headline: Drillers rally breaks on Transocean EPS outlook.

text.p: Oil drilling stocks snapped a week long rally after Transocean Offshore Inc announced that second quarter earnings would be $0.10 per share lower than analysts' forecasts.
Transocean itself was off 1-7/8, 2.49 percent, at 73-1/2 in volume of 312,700 shares.
However, analysts said that they thought the earnings warning was specific to Transocean and that the fundamentals of the sector remained intact.
"We have just seen one of the most spectacular rallies that this group has ever seen, so it is not surprising there is some sort of pullback," said Jamie Stone, analyst at Schroder & Co.
He noted that even after the Transocean news, the stock was down just $2 and that among the rest of the sector, stocks were generally off around $1.
Out of the 20 drilling and service companies Stone follows, 18 are rated "buy" or better, he said.
"Fundamentals in the sector continue to get better, rigs are being contracted at higher dayrates and oil companies are talking very positively spending in 1997 and 1998," Stone said.
Among other stocks, Falcon Drilling Co Inc was off 1 at 58-1/4, Pride International Inc shed 0-3/4 to 23-3/4, Ensco International down 1-1/8 58-5/8.
